question.sl: Ali lahko psi jedo ovsene kosmiče?

answer.en: Yes, in small amounts. Plain oatmeal, cooked with water rather than milk, is fine for dogs. Never give flavoured or instant oatmeal, and leave out salt, butter, chocolate and raisins.
answer.sl: Da, v majhnih količinah. Navadna ovsena kaša, kuhana z vodo namesto z mlekom, je za pse v redu. Nikoli ne dajajte aromatizirane ali instant kaše in ne dodajajte soli, masla, čokolade ali rozin.

why.en: Oatmeal is high in fibre, including soluble fibre that can help dogs with irregular bowel movements. But dogs digest dairy poorly, raw oats are harder to digest, and a lot of fibre can cause stomach upset, diarrhoea and vomiting; a large amount can even lead to bloat. It is also fairly high in carbs and calories. Flavoured oatmeal often has more sugar and may contain xylitol, which is toxic to dogs, and instant oatmeal is highly processed.
why.sl: Ovseni kosmiči imajo veliko vlaknin, tudi topnih, ki lahko pomagajo psom z neredno prebavo. Toda psi slabo prebavljajo mlečne izdelke, surovi kosmiči so težje prebavljivi, veliko vlaknin pa lahko povzroči prebavne težave, drisko in bruhanje; velika količina lahko celo povzroči napihnjenost želodca. Imajo tudi precej ogljikovih hidratov in kalorij. Aromatizirana kaša ima pogosto več sladkorja in lahko vsebuje ksilitol, ki je za pse strupen, instant kaša pa je močno predelana.

what_to_do.en: Introduce it gradually and watch how your dog handles it. If your dog seems to react badly, contact your vet straight away.
what_to_do.sl: Ovseno kašo uvajajte postopoma in opazujte, kako jo pes prenaša. Če se zdi, da se nanjo slabo odziva, takoj pokličite veterinarja.

serving.en: Plain, cooked oatmeal made with water, not milk, and not too much at once. Not raw, not instant, and no sugar, salt, butter, chocolate, raisins or flavourings.
serving.sl: Navadna kuhana ovsena kaša, pripravljena z vodo, ne z mlekom, in ne preveč naenkrat. Ne surova, ne instant, brez sladkorja, soli, masla, čokolade, rozin in arom.

child.en: Dogs can have a little plain oatmeal made with water. Sweet or flavoured porridge is not for dogs.
child.sl: Psi lahko dobijo malo navadne ovsene kaše, kuhane z vodo. Sladka ali aromatizirana kaša ni za pse.

q.sl: Ali lahko psi jedo surove ovsene kosmiče?

a.en: It's better to cook them. Raw oats sprinkled over food are only harder for your dog to digest.
a.sl: Bolje jih je skuhati. Surovi kosmiči, posuti po hrani, so za psa le težje prebavljivi.

q.en: Is flavoured instant oatmeal safe for dogs?
q.sl: Je aromatizirana instant kaša za pse varna?

a.en: No. Flavoured oatmeal often has extra sugar and may contain xylitol, which is toxic to dogs, and instant oatmeal is highly processed.
a.sl: Ne. Aromatizirana kaša ima pogosto dodan sladkor in lahko vsebuje ksilitol, ki je za pse strupen, instant kaša pa je močno predelana.

sources.quote: The answer is yes, but there are some things you should keep in mind before feeding your dog this snack.
Oatmeal is high in fiber and contains a plethora of nutrients, minerals, and antioxidants.
It's also a great source of soluble fiber, which can regulate blood glucose levels
and help dogs that have irregular bowl movements.
When preparing oatmeal for your dog, make it with water, as opposed to milk.
Dogs are very sensitive to dairy, and their bodies don't break down lactose as easily as humans do,
If you plan to share your oatmeal, make sure it's cooked and not sprinkled raw over food
serving it raw will only make it harder for your pup to digest.
It should also be plain.
While humans might enjoy additives, such as salt, butter, chocolate, raisins, or grapes,
these ingredients can be extremely harmful to a dog's health.
Never feed your dog flavored oatmeal, as it often contains more sugar and may even have artificial sweeteners,
such as xylitol, which is toxic to dogs.
Dr. Fox also advises owners to stay away from instant oatmeal.
While it's faster and easier to prepare, it's highly processed,
But Dr. Fox cautions that feeding your dog foods containing a lot of fiber can lead to GI upset, diarrhea, and vomiting.
Consuming a large amount can also lead to diarrhea, vomiting, or bloat, which can be life threatening.
Don't give your dog too much oatmeal at once because it contains a lot of carbohydrates
is relatively high in calories.
When introducing human food into your dog's diet, start off gradually and gauge how well they handle it.
If they appear to have an adverse reaction, consult your veterinarian immediately.
